```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	YouTube Playlist Ingestion Pipeline
4	
5	Takes one or more YouTube podcast playlist URLs, enumerates every episode,
6	and drives each one through the full Disclosure RAG pipeline:
7	
8	  playlist URL(s)
9	    -> episode enumeration (yt-dlp flat extraction, pytube fallback)
10	    -> transcript fetch (lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced, cookie-free)
11	    -> transcript parse + clean (lib/transcript_fidelity.clean_transcript)
12	    -> fidelity review (lib/transcript_fidelity.review_transcript, optional LLM pass)
13	    -> quality gate (fail/below threshold -> quarantined for human review)
14	    -> main.process_url() -> KB storage, Upstash sync, NER entity extraction,
15	       vectorization (--upload -> OpenAI vector store), CocoIndex knowledge
16	       graph, Mem0 memory
17	
18	Every episode outcome is checkpointed to a state file, so re-running the same
19	playlist resumes where it left off. Per-episode transcripts and fidelity
20	reports are saved under data/playlist_ingestion/ alongside a markdown run
21	report.
22	
23	Usage (from apps/disclosure-rag/, venv active, .env loaded):
24	
25	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <PLAYLIST_URL> [<PLAYLIST_URL> ...]
26	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py --from-file playlists.txt --upload
27	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --limit 5 --dry-run
28	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --llm-review --min-fidelity 0.6
29	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --force        # reprocess all
30	"""
31	
32	import argparse
33	import json
34	import logging
35	import os
36	import re
37	import sys
38	import time
39	from datetime import datetime, timezone
40	from pathlib import Path
41	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
42	
43	sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
44	
45	from lib.transcript_fidelity import clean_transcript, review_transcript
46	
47	logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
48	logger = logging.getLogger("playlist_ingestion")
49	
50	BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
51	OUTPUT_DIR = BASE_DIR / "data" / "playlist_ingestion"
52	DEFAULT_STATE_FILE = OUTPUT_DIR / "state.json"
53	
54	# Terminal states that --force is required to reprocess
55	DONE_STATUSES = {"ingested", "quarantined"}
56	
57	
58	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- enumeration
59	
60	def enumerate_playlist(playlist_url: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
61	    """Return {playlist_id, title, videos: [{video_id, url, title, duration}]}.
62	
63	    Tries yt-dlp flat extraction first (fast, no downloads, includes per-entry
64	    durations), then falls back to pytube. A plain video URL is treated as a
65	    single-episode playlist.
66	    """
67	    try:
68	        import yt_dlp
69	        opts = {"quiet": True, "no_warnings": True, "extract_flat": "in_playlist", "skip_download": True}
70	        with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
71	            # process=False skips format resolution entirely — metadata only,
72	            # works for playlists AND single videos even on older yt-dlp
73	            info = ydl.extract_info(playlist_url, download=False, process=False)
74	        entries = info.get("entries")
75	        entries = list(entries) if entries is not None else [info]  # generator when process=False
76	        videos = []
77	        for e in entries:
78	            if not e:
79	                continue
80	            vid = e.get("id")
81	            if not vid:
82	                continue
83	            videos.append({
84	                "video_id": vid,
85	                "url": f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}",
86	                "title": e.get("title") or vid,
87	                "duration": e.get("duration"),
88	                "uploader": e.get("uploader") or e.get("channel"),
89	            })
90	        return {
91	            "playlist_id": info.get("id") or "unknown",
92	            "title": info.get("title") or playlist_url,
93	            "videos": videos,
94	        }
95	    except Exception as e:
96	        logger.warning(f"yt-dlp enumeration failed ({e}); trying pytube")
97	
98	    try:
99	        from pytube import Playlist
100	        pl = Playlist(playlist_url)
101	        videos = []
102	        for url in pl.video_urls:
103	            m = re.search(r"[?&]v=([\w-]{6,})", url)
104	            if m:
105	                videos.append({"video_id": m.group(1), "url": url, "title": m.group(1), "duration": None,
106	                               "uploader": None})
107	        return {"playlist_id": getattr(pl, "playlist_id", "unknown"),
108	                "title": getattr(pl, "title", playlist_url), "videos": videos}
109	    except Exception as e:
110	        logger.error(f"Could not enumerate playlist {playlist_url}: {e}")
111	        return {"playlist_id": "unknown", "title": playlist_url, "videos": []}
112	
113	
114	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- state
115	
116	def load_state(state_file: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
117	    if state_file.exists():
118	        try:
119	            return json.loads(state_file.read_text())
120	        except Exception as e:
121	            logger.warning(f"State file unreadable, starting fresh: {e}")
122	    return {"videos": {}}
123	
124	
125	def save_state(state: Dict[str, Any], state_file: Path) -> None:
126	    state_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
127	    tmp = state_file.with_suffix(".tmp")
128	    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
129	    tmp.replace(state_file)
130	
131	
132	def record(state: Dict[str, Any], video: Dict[str, Any], playlist_id: str, **fields) -> None:
133	    entry = state["videos"].setdefault(video["video_id"], {})
134	    entry.update({
135	        "title": video.get("title"),
136	        "url": video.get("url"),
137	        "playlist_id": playlist_id,
138	        "updated": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
139	        **fields,
140	    })
141	
142	
143	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-episode
144	
145	def fetch_transcript(url: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
146	    """Fetch transcript + metadata via the cookie-free transcript-api path."""
147	    try:
148	        from lib.youtube_transcript_enhanced import get_metadata_and_transcript_api_first
149	        result = get_metadata_and_transcript_api_first(url)
150	        if result.get("ok") and result.get("transcript"):
151	            return result
152	        return None
153	    except Exception as e:
154	        logger.warning(f"Transcript fetch failed for {url}: {e}")
155	        return None
156	
157	
158	def process_episode(video: Dict[str, Any], playlist_id: str, state: Dict[str, Any],
159	                    args: argparse.Namespace, transcripts_dir: Path, reports_dir: Path) -> str:
160	    """Run one episode through fetch -> parse -> fidelity gate -> pipeline.
161	
162	    Returns the resulting status string.
163	    """
164	    vid, url = video["video_id"], video["url"]
165	
166	    fetched = fetch_transcript(url)
167	    if not fetched:
168	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="no_transcript")
169	        return "no_transcript"
170	
171	    raw_transcript = fetched["transcript"]
172	    cleaned = clean_transcript(raw_transcript)
173	    transcripts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
174	    (transcripts_dir / f"{vid}.txt").write_text(
175	        f"{fetched.get('title') or video['title']}\n{url}\n\n{cleaned}", encoding="utf-8")
176	
177	    fidelity = review_transcript(
178	        transcript=raw_transcript,
179	        video_id=vid,
180	        segments=fetched.get("transcript_segments"),
181	        expected_duration_seconds=video.get("duration"),
182	        use_llm=args.llm_review,
183	    )
184	    reports_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
185	    (reports_dir / f"{vid}.fidelity.json").write_text(
186	        json.dumps(fidelity.to_dict(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
187	
188	    logger.info(f"  fidelity {fidelity.score:.2f} ({fidelity.verdict}) — {video['title'][:70]}")
189	
190	    if fidelity.verdict == "fail" or fidelity.score < args.min_fidelity:
191	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="quarantined",
192	               fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict,
193	               issues=fidelity.issues[:5])
194	        return "quarantined"
195	
196	    if args.dry_run:
197	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="dry_run",
198	               fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict)
199	        return "dry_run"
200	
201	    # Full pipeline: KB storage, Upstash sync, NER, vectorize, CocoIndex KG, Mem0
202	    try:
203	        from main import process_url
204	        result = process_url(url, upload=args.upload, add_to_kb=not args.no_kb)
205	        if result and result.get("doc_id"):
206	            record(state, video, playlist_id, status="ingested",
207	                   fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict,
208	                   doc_id=result["doc_id"])
209	            return "ingested"
210	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="failed",
211	               fidelity=fidelity.score, error="pipeline returned no doc_id")
212	        return "failed"
213	    except Exception as e:
214	        logger.error(f"Pipeline error for {vid}: {e}")
215	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="failed",
216	               fidelity=fidelity.score, error=str(e))
217	        return "failed"
218	
219	
220	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- run report
221	
222	def write_run_report(runs: List[Dict[str, Any]], counts: Dict[str, int], reports_dir: Path) -> Path:
223	    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
224	    lines = [f"# Playlist Ingestion Run — {ts} UTC", ""]
225	    lines.append("| Status | Count |")
226	    lines.append("|--------|-------|")
227	    for status, n in sorted(counts.items()):
228	        lines.append(f"| {status} | {n} |")
229	    lines.append("")
230	    for run in runs:
231	        lines.append(f"## {run['title']} (`{run['playlist_id']}`)")
232	        lines.append("")
233	        lines.append("| Episode | Status | Fidelity | Doc ID |")
234	        lines.append("|---------|--------|----------|--------|")
235	        for ep in run["episodes"]:
236	            lines.append(f"| {ep['title'][:60]} | {ep['status']} | {ep.get('fidelity', '—')} | {ep.get('doc_id', '—')} |")
237	        lines.append("")
238	    reports_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
239	    path = reports_dir / f"run-{ts}.md"
240	    path.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
241	    return path
242	
243	
244	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main
245	
246	def main() -> int:
247	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Ingest YouTube podcast playlists into the Disclosure RAG pipeline")
248	    parser.add_argument("playlists", nargs="*", help="One or more playlist (or video) URLs")
249	    parser.add_argument("--from-file", help="File with one playlist URL per line (# comments allowed)")
250	    parser.add_argument("--upload", action="store_true", help="Upload to OpenAI vector store (vectorization)")
251	    parser.add_argument("--no-kb", action="store_true", help="Skip knowledge base storage")
252	    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="Max new episodes to process per playlist")
253	    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="Reprocess episodes already in the state file")
254	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Fetch + fidelity-review only; no ingestion")
255	    parser.add_argument("--min-fidelity", type=float, default=0.45,
256	                        help="Minimum fidelity score to ingest (default 0.45; below -> quarantined)")
257	    parser.add_argument("--llm-review", action="store_true",
258	                        help="Add LLM coherence pass to fidelity review (uses FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL)")
259	    parser.add_argument("--delay", type=float, default=2.0, help="Seconds between episodes (default 2)")
260	    parser.add_argument("--state-file", default=str(DEFAULT_STATE_FILE), help="Checkpoint state file path")
261	    args = parser.parse_args()
262	
263	    urls = list(args.playlists)
264	    if args.from_file:
265	        for line in Path(args.from_file).read_text().splitlines():
266	            line = line.strip()
267	            if line and not line.startswith("#"):
268	                urls.append(line)
269	    if not urls:
270	        parser.error("No playlist URLs given (positional args or --from-file)")
271	
272	    state_file = Path(args.state_file)
273	    state = load_state(state_file)
274	    transcripts_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / "transcripts"
275	    reports_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / "reports"
276	
277	    counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
278	    runs: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
279	
280	    for playlist_url in urls:
281	        logger.info(f"Enumerating playlist: {playlist_url}")
282	        playlist = enumerate_playlist(playlist_url)
283	        videos = playlist["videos"]
284	        logger.info(f"Playlist '{playlist['title']}': {len(videos)} episodes")
285	        if not videos:
286	            counts["enumeration_failed"] = counts.get("enumeration_failed", 0) + 1
287	            continue
288	
289	        run: Dict[str, Any] = {"playlist_id": playlist["playlist_id"], "title": playlist["title"], "episodes": []}
290	        processed = 0
291	        for i, video in enumerate(videos, 1):
292	            vid = video["video_id"]
293	            existing = state["videos"].get(vid, {})
294	            if not args.force and existing.get("status") in DONE_STATUSES:
295	                logger.info(f"[{i}/{len(videos)}] skip (already {existing['status']}): {video['title'][:70]}")
296	                counts["skipped"] = counts.get("skipped", 0) + 1
297	                continue
298	            if args.limit and processed >= args.limit:
299	                logger.info(f"--limit {args.limit} reached for this playlist")
300	                break
301	
302	            logger.info(f"[{i}/{len(videos)}] processing: {video['title'][:70]}")
303	            status = process_episode(video, playlist["playlist_id"], state, args, transcripts_dir, reports_dir)
304	            counts[status] = counts.get(status, 0) + 1
305	            processed += 1
306	            save_state(state, state_file)
307	
308	            entry = state["videos"].get(vid, {})
309	            run["episodes"].append({"title": video["title"], "status": status,
310	                                    "fidelity": entry.get("fidelity"), "doc_id": entry.get("doc_id")})
311	            if args.delay and i < len(videos):
312	                time.sleep(args.delay)
313	        runs.append(run)
314	
315	    report_path = write_run_report(runs, counts, reports_dir)
316	    logger.info(f"Run report: {report_path}")
317	    logger.info(f"Summary: {json.dumps(counts)}")
318	    return 0 if not counts.get("failed") else 1
319	
320	
321	if __name__ == "__main__":
322	    sys.exit(main())
```

```text
"""Single definition of "did LLM enrichment actually happen on this run?".

Every ingestion path produces a `rag_pipeline` block, but files it in a
different place, so grading it needs one search order that knows all of them.
This lived inside scripts/playlist_ingestion.py, where only the playlist path
could reach it — main.py's direct `dy <url>` path had no gate at all and
reported success on a run whose retrieval layer came back empty.

main.py cannot import from scripts/ (playlist_ingestion imports main, so it
would be circular), which is why this is a lib module rather than a helper
shared by proximity.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Tuple

#: Statuses from RagPipelineResult that mean enrichment genuinely succeeded.
OK_STATUSES = {"ok"}
#: Statuses that are a deliberate, recorded decision — not a failure.
HELD_STATUSES = {"hold", "rejected", "skipped"}
```

```text
357	    if args.from_file:

373	    aborted = False

382	        if not videos:

384	            continue

406	            run["episodes"].append({"title": video["title"], "status": status,
407	                                    "fidelity": entry.get("fidelity"), "doc_id": entry.get("doc_id")})
408	
409	            # Only a status that required YouTube to actually serve us caption
410	            # data clears the counter. `unavailable` must not: a private video
411	            # fails before any transcript request, so treating it as evidence
412	            # that egress works lets a playlist with private episodes sprinkled
413	            # through it reset the breaker forever while every real fetch fails.
414	            if status == "blocked":
415	                consecutive_blocked += 1
416	            elif status != "unavailable":
417	                consecutive_blocked = 0
418	            if consecutive_blocked >= BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD:
419	                from lib.youtube_transcript_enhanced import proxy_configured
420	                logger.error(
421	                    "Aborting: YouTube blocked %d consecutive transcript requests. This is an "
422	                    "IP-level block, not a property of these videos — continuing would record "
423	                    "the rest of the playlist as failures. Remedy: %s, then re-run (blocked "
424	                    "episodes are not terminal and will be retried).",
425	                    consecutive_blocked,
426	                    "rotate the proxy / wait out the block" if proxy_configured()
427	                    else "set YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_USERNAME + YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_PASSWORD (or YT_PROXY_URL)")
428	                aborted = True
429	                break
430	
431	            if args.delay and i < len(videos):
432	                time.sleep(args.delay)
433	        runs.append(run)
434	
435	    report_path = write_run_report(runs, counts, reports_dir)
436	    logger.info(f"Run report: {report_path}")
437	    logger.info(f"Summary: {json.dumps(counts)}")
438	    if aborted:
439	        return 2
440	    return 0 if not counts.get("failed") else 1
```

```text
136	        "url": video.get("url"),

145	def fetch_transcript(url: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
146	    """Fetch transcript + metadata via the cookie-free transcript-api path."""
147	    try:

149	        result = get_metadata_and_transcript_api_first(url)
150	        if result.get("ok") and result.get("transcript"):

152	        return None
153	    except Exception as e:

158	def process_episode(video: Dict[str, Any], playlist_id: str, state: Dict[str, Any],
159	                    args: argparse.Namespace, transcripts_dir: Path, reports_dir: Path) -> str:
160	    """Run one episode through fetch -> parse -> fidelity gate -> pipeline.
161	
162	    Returns the resulting status string.
163	    """
164	    vid, url = video["video_id"], video["url"]
165	
166	    fetched = fetch_transcript(url)
167	    if not fetched:
168	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="no_transcript")
169	        return "no_transcript"
170	
171	    raw_transcript = fetched["transcript"]
172	    cleaned = clean_transcript(raw_transcript)
173	    transcripts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
174	    (transcripts_dir / f"{vid}.txt").write_text(
175	        f"{fetched.get('title') or video['title']}\n{url}\n\n{cleaned}", encoding="utf-8")
176	
177	    fidelity = review_transcript(
178	        transcript=raw_transcript,
179	        video_id=vid,
180	        segments=fetched.get("transcript_segments"),
181	        expected_duration_seconds=video.get("duration"),
182	        use_llm=args.llm_review,
183	    )
184	    reports_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
185	    (reports_dir / f"{vid}.fidelity.json").write_text(
186	        json.dumps(fidelity.to_dict(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
187	
188	    logger.info(f"  fidelity {fidelity.score:.2f} ({fidelity.verdict}) — {video['title'][:70]}")
189	
190	    if fidelity.verdict == "fail" or fidelity.score < args.min_fidelity:
191	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="quarantined",
192	               fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict,
193	               issues=fidelity.issues[:5])
194	        return "quarantined"
195	
196	    if args.dry_run:
197	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="dry_run",
198	               fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict)
199	        return "dry_run"
```

```text
"""Single Postgres connection point for disclosure-rag.

Modeled on packages/db/scripts/rebuild/db_ops.py: plain psycopg (v3), one
DATABASE_URL, no ORM. The URL must point at the shared Neon endpoint that
packages/db owns (the same database apps/app reads) so ingested data lands
in the knowledge graph the rest of the platform actually uses.

Usage:
    from lib.db import connect

    with connect() as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM documents")
        print(cur.fetchone()[0])

Environment resolution order:
    1. DATABASE_URL already in the process environment (set by main.sh /
       run.sh sourcing apps/disclosure-rag/.env)
    2. packages/db/.env at the monorepo root, as a fallback so scripts run
       from this workspace agree with the canonical connection string
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from pathlib import Path

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_PACKAGES_DB_ENV = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3].parent / "packages" / "db" / ".env"
)


def _read_url_from_env_file(env_path: Path) -> str | None:
    """Pull DATABASE_URL out of a dotenv file without mutating os.environ.

    Uses python-dotenv's parser so `export DATABASE_URL=...`, quoted values,
    and inline comments all behave the way the shell would treat them.
    """
    if not env_path.is_file():
        return None
    from dotenv import dotenv_values
    return dotenv_values(env_path).get("DATABASE_URL") or None


def _host_of(url: str) -> str:
    """Best-effort host extraction for log messages - never logs credentials."""
    try:
        return url.split("@", 1)[1].split("/", 1)[0]
    except IndexError:
        return "<unparseable>"


def get_database_url() -> str:
    """Resolve the shared Postgres connection string.

    Raises RuntimeError (not sys.exit - this is a library, callers decide
    how to die) when no URL can be found anywhere.
    """
    url = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL")
    if url:
        return url

    url = _read_url_from_env_file(_PACKAGES_DB_ENV)
    if url:
        # Loud on purpose: this fallback silently retargets code that may
        # previously have pointed at localhost onto the SHARED Neon database.
        logger.warning(
            "DATABASE_URL not in environment - falling back to "
            "packages/db/.env (host: %s). This is the LIVE shared database; "
            "source apps/disclosure-rag/.env if you intended a different "
            "target.", _host_of(url)
        )
        return url

    raise RuntimeError(
        "DATABASE_URL not set. Source apps/disclosure-rag/.env or ensure "
        f"{_PACKAGES_DB_ENV} exists - both must point at the shared Neon "
        "endpoint used by packages/db."
    )


def connect(autocommit: bool = False, read_only: bool = False):
    """Open a psycopg (v3) connection to the shared database.

    Returned connection is a context manager; use `with connect() as conn:`
    so transactions commit/rollback deterministically.

    Pass read_only=True for stats/inspection callers - it marks the psycopg
    session read-only so an accidental write raises instead of mutating the
```

```text
=== full lib/enrichment_status.py ===
"""Single definition of "did LLM enrichment actually happen on this run?".

Every ingestion path produces a `rag_pipeline` block, but files it in a
different place, so grading it needs one search order that knows all of them.
This lived inside scripts/playlist_ingestion.py, where only the playlist path
could reach it — main.py's direct `dy <url>` path had no gate at all and
reported success on a run whose retrieval layer came back empty.

main.py cannot import from scripts/ (playlist_ingestion imports main, so it
would be circular), which is why this is a lib module rather than a helper
shared by proximity.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Tuple

#: Statuses from RagPipelineResult that mean enrichment genuinely succeeded.
OK_STATUSES = {"ok"}
#: Statuses that are a deliberate, recorded decision — not a failure.
HELD_STATUSES = {"hold", "rejected", "skipped"}


def enrichment_outcome(result: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """Grade LLM enrichment from a process_url/process_file result.

    Returns (status, error_detail).

    The status lives in a different place depending on which path ran:
    `process_file` sets `result['rag_pipeline']` and
    `result['metadata']['rag_pipeline']`; the YouTube path (lib/youtube.py)
    files it under the transcript's file metadata and
    knowledge_base_service surfaces it at both levels.

    Returns "unknown" when no signal is found. That matters: reporting
    `ingested` on absence is precisely how a run of documents whose enrichment
    had 401'd got recorded as successful.
    """
    for container in (result, result.get("metadata") or {}, result.get("file_metadata") or {}):
        rag = container.get("rag_pipeline") if isinstance(container, dict) else None
        if isinstance(rag, dict) and rag.get("status"):
            return rag["status"], "; ".join(rag.get("errors") or [])[:300]

    for stage in result.get("stage_report") or []:
        if isinstance(stage, dict) and "RAG prompt pipeline" in (stage.get("name") or ""):
            raw = stage.get("status") or "unknown"
            return {"success": "ok", "failed": "error"}.get(raw, raw), (stage.get("detail") or "")[:300]

    return "unknown", ""
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
class KnowledgeBaseCRUD:
    """Enhanced CRUD operations for the knowledge base"""

    def __init__(self, kb_path: Optional[str] = None):
        # Use the packages/knowledge-base workspace, not a local knowledge-base directory.
        #
        # DISCLOSURE_RAG_KB_PATH overrides the root for the whole process. Without it
        # there is no way to exercise the real write path without mutating the
        # production archive, because kb_service constructs its CRUD with no argument
        # (lib/knowledge_base_service.py:50). The benchmark harness
        # (scripts/benchmark_pipeline.py) sets it to a temp dir so ingest checks run
        # against a sandbox archive. Explicit kb_path still wins over the env var.
        self.kb_path = Path(kb_path or os.environ.get("DISCLOSURE_RAG_KB_PATH") or os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(
                os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__)))),
            "packages", "knowledge-base"
        ))
        self.metadata_path = self.kb_path / "metadata"
        self.sources_path = self.kb_path / "sources"
        self.files_path = self.sources_path / "files"
        self.transcripts_path = self.sources_path / "transcripts"
        self.articles_path = self.sources_path / "web"
        self.research_path = self.kb_path / "research"

        # Create directories if they don't exist
        for path in [self.metadata_path, self.sources_path, self.files_path,
                     self.transcripts_path, self.articles_path, self.research_path]:
            path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # Initialize metadata index
        self.index_file = self.metadata_path / "index.json"
        self._init_index()

    def _init_index(self):
        """Initialize or load the document index"""
        if not self.index_file.exists():
            self.index = {"documents": {}, "tags": {}, "last_updated": ""}
            self._save_index()
        else:
            with open(self.index_file, 'r') as f:
                self.index = json.load(f)

    def _save_index(self):
        """Save the index to disk atomically.

        Writes to a temp file in the same directory then `os.replace()`s it
        onto the target, so a crash mid-write can never leave index.json
        truncated or partially written (mirrors the pattern in
        scripts/playlist_ingestion.py::save_state).
        """
        self.index["last_updated"] = datetime.now().isoformat()
        tmp_file = self.index_file.parent / f"{self.index_file.name}.tmp"
        with open(tmp_file, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(self.index, f, indent=2)
        os.replace(tmp_file, self.index_file)

    @contextmanager
    def _locked_index(self):
        """Exclusive OS-level lock spanning an index read-modify-write cycle.

        Acquires an flock() on a dedicated lock file (not index.json itself,
        so readers/writers never fight over the atomic-replace target), then
        reloads self.index from disk while holding the lock so this process
        observes any writes made by other concurrent processes/instances
        instead of trusting a possibly-stale in-memory copy. Callers should
        do all of their index reads *and* writes inside this context.

        Only the methods in this file that perform create/update/delete use
```

 `./apps/disclosure-rag/lib/llm_fallback.py`

```text
1	"""Multi-provider frontier-model fallback chain for disclosure-rag enrichment.
2	
3	Python counterpart to `apps/app/src/lib/ai/model-fallback.ts`. Same policy:
4	only current frontier models, never legacy tiers. Tiers are tried in order, a
5	tier is skipped when its credential is absent, and the chain moves on when a
6	tier errors — so one provider being down never takes enrichment down.
7	
8	Two things this adds over the TS version, because this side runs *batches*
9	(104 podcast episodes x several prompts each) rather than one interactive
10	stream:
11	
12	1. **Error classification.** A 401/403/404 is permanent — the tier is marked
13	   dead for the life of the process and skipped thereafter, so a revoked key
14	   costs one wasted round-trip per run instead of one per call. A 429/5xx/
15	   timeout is transient and gets a bounded retry with backoff.
16	2. **Attribution.** `complete()` returns which tier served the request, so
17	   callers can record truthfully whether enrichment actually happened. Silent
18	   degradation is how a whole ingestion run once recorded `status: ingested`
19	   on documents whose enrichment had 401'd.
20	
21	**Gateway policy (2026-08-07).** First-party OpenAI and Anthropic tiers were
22	removed from this chain, not demoted. A trailing tier is still a *reachable*
23	tier: leaving one in place means the first time every gateway above it fails,
24	the run silently bills a vendor we have chosen to stop paying. Absence is the
25	only enforcement that survives an outage. `AllProvidersFailed` raising is the
26	intended behaviour when the gateways are down.
27	
28	Consequence worth stating plainly: enrichment no longer has an OpenAI or
29	Anthropic safety net, so a total gateway outage now fails the run instead of
30	quietly costing money. That is the trade the policy asks for.
31	
32	Note this governs *completions only*. Embeddings remain on OpenAI
33	`text-embedding-3-small` @ 1536 dims — 6,540 vectors are already stored in
34	Postgres against that model, and re-providering them does not error, it
35	silently returns incoherent rankings. See `lib/knowledge_base.py:127,172`.
36	
37	Credential liveness verified 2026-08-07 against each provider's models
38	endpoint (see CHAIN comments). A 200 there proves only that the endpoint
39	lists models — it is not proof of credit, which is how a chain of "live"
40	tiers once produced 47 consecutive `enrichment_failed` episodes. Dead-keyed
41	tiers below the gateways are deliberately retained: they cost one attempt per
42	process and light up automatically once the credential is fixed.
43	"""
44	
45	from __future__ import annotations
46	
47	import json
48	import logging
49	import os
50	import random
51	import time
52	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
53	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence
54	
55	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
56	
57	# Status codes that mean "this tier will never work in this process".
58	#
59	# 402 earns its place empirically: on 2026-08-07 the HuggingFace router
60	# answered a live completion with `402 - You have depleted your monthly
61	# included credits`. Depleted credit does not un-deplete mid-run, but 402 was
62	# in neither set, so it fell through to the transient path and would have cost
63	# one wasted round-trip on *every* call across a 104-episode batch — precisely
64	# the per-call waste this module's docstring claims to have designed out.
65	PERMANENT_STATUS = {400, 401, 402, 403, 404}
66	# Status codes worth retrying on the same tier before moving on.
67	TRANSIENT_STATUS = {408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
68	
69	DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE = 0.1
70	DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 1200
71	
72	
73	@dataclass(frozen=True)
74	class Tier:
75	    """One attempt in the fallback chain.
76	
77	    `kind` selects the wire protocol, not the vendor: "anthropic" uses the
78	    Anthropic Messages API, "openai_compat" uses OpenAI's chat/completions
79	    shape, which DeepSeek, Together, Groq, and z.ai all serve. That keeps the
80	    dependency surface at two SDKs (both already installed) instead of one per
81	    provider.
82	    """
83	
84	    id: str
85	    provider: str
86	    env_keys: Sequence[str]
87	    model: str
88	    kind: str = "openai_compat"
89	    base_url: Optional[str] = None
90	    max_retries: int = 0
91	    #: Model emits chain-of-thought before its answer, billed against the same
92	    #: max_tokens budget. Verified 2026-08-07: deepseek-v4-pro and Kimi-K3 both
93	    #: return finish_reason="length" with EMPTY content at max_tokens=16, and
94	    #: the correct answer at 800 — the reasoning ate the entire budget. Without
95	    #: a floor this looks exactly like a broken provider. (Same class of trap
96	    #: as Gemini's thinkingBudget in the TS chain.)
97	    reasoning: bool = False
98	
99	    def api_key(self) -> Optional[str]:
100	        for key in self.env_keys:
101	            value = os.environ.get(key)
102	            if value:
103	                return value
104	        return None
105	
106	
107	#: Extra budget *added* for reasoning tiers so chain-of-thought cannot starve
108	#: the answer.
109	#:
110	#: This was a `max(max_tokens, 2048)` floor until 2026-08-07. A floor is the
111	#: wrong shape: it caps CoT and answer under one ceiling, so a caller asking
112	#: for 1200 tokens of JSON got 2048 total and the reasoning ate the difference.
113	#: Observed directly when GLM-5.2 became tier 1 — a real 20k-char transcript
114	#: produced JSON that truncated mid-token at char 7209 and failed to parse.
115	#: Headroom is additive because the caller's number describes the *answer* it
116	#: needs; the model's thinking is a separate cost the caller cannot size.
117	REASONING_HEADROOM_TOKENS = 4096
118	
119	
120	# Ordering rationale: three gateways first, then direct-vendor tiers as a
121	# long tail. The gateways all serve **the same model** (GLM-5.2, the one entry
122	# on the frontier-only list that is neither OpenAI nor Anthropic), so falling
123	# from tier 1 to tier 3 is a change of *route*, not a change of capability —
124	# enrichment quality does not silently degrade as the chain descends, which is
125	# what a mixed-capability chain would do.
126	#
127	# All three speak OpenAI's chat/completions shape, so this needs no new SDK.
128	FRONTIER_FALLBACK_CHAIN: List[Tier] = [
129	    Tier(
130	        # Endpoint verified 200 on 2026-08-07. Serves `z-ai/glm-5.2`.
131	        # Key lives in the repo-root .env and was invisible here until it was
132	        # copied into apps/disclosure-rag/.env — this app calls bare
133	        # load_dotenv(), whose find_dotenv() stops at the first .env going up.
134	        id="openrouter/glm-5.2",
135	        provider="GLM-5.2 (OpenRouter)",
136	        env_keys=("OPENROUTER_API_KEY",),
137	        model="z-ai/glm-5.2",
138	        base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
139	        max_retries=1,
140	        reasoning=True,
141	    ),
142	    Tier(
143	        # Endpoint verified 200 on 2026-08-07. Serves `zai-org/GLM-5.2`.
144	        # Credential is currently **ambient shell state only** — exported in
145	        # the user's profile, absent from every .env in the repo. That means
146	        # this tier is live for an interactive `dy` run and silently skipped
147	        # under cron/CI, which is exactly the kind of environment-dependent
148	        # behaviour that makes a fallback chain untrustworthy. Move it into
149	        # apps/disclosure-rag/.env to make it real everywhere.
150	        id="huggingface/glm-5.2",
151	        provider="GLM-5.2 (HuggingFace Router)",
152	        env_keys=("HUGGINGFACE_ACCESS_TOKEN", "HF_TOKEN", "HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY"),
153	        model="zai-org/GLM-5.2",
154	        base_url="https://router.huggingface.co/v1",
155	        max_retries=1,
156	        reasoning=True,
157	    ),
158	    Tier(
159	        # Endpoint verified 200 on 2026-08-07. Serves bare `glm-5.2`.
160	        # Same ambient-only caveat as the HuggingFace tier: exported from
161	        # ~/.zshrc, not present in any .env.
162	        id="ollama-cloud/glm-5.2",
163	        provider="GLM-5.2 (Ollama Cloud)",
164	        env_keys=("OLLAMA_API_KEY",),
165	        model="glm-5.2",
166	        base_url="https://ollama.com/v1",
167	        max_retries=1,
168	        reasoning=True,
169	    ),
170	    Tier(
171	        # Live 2026-08-07. First tier on a different vendor + credential.
172	        id="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
173	        provider="DeepSeek V4 Pro",
174	        env_keys=("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY",),
175	        model="deepseek-v4-pro",
176	        base_url="https://api.deepseek.com",
177	        max_retries=1,
178	        reasoning=True,
179	    ),
180	    Tier(
181	        # Live 2026-08-07. Third distinct vendor.
182	        id="together/kimi-k3",
183	        provider="Kimi K3 (Together)",
184	        env_keys=("TOGETHERAI_API_KEY", "TOGETHER_API_KEY"),
185	        model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3",
186	        base_url="https://api.together.xyz/v1",
187	        max_retries=1,
188	        reasoning=True,
189	    ),
190	    Tier(
191	        # Key returned 401 on 2026-08-07. Retained: costs one attempt per
192	        # process, activates when fixed. `openai/gpt-oss-120b` is an
193	        # open-weight model served by Groq — it uses a Groq credential and
194	        # bills Groq, so it is not OpenAI API usage despite the model name.
195	        id="groq/gpt-oss-120b",
196	        provider="GPT-OSS 120B (Groq)",
197	        env_keys=("GROQ_API_KEY",),
198	        model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
199	        base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
200	    ),
201	    Tier(
202	        # No ZHIPU_API_KEY/GLM_API_KEY in this app's env — skipped for free,
203	        # present so parity with the TS chain is explicit rather than an
204	        # oversight.
205	        id="zhipu/glm-5.2",
206	        provider="GLM-5.2",
207	        env_keys=("ZHIPU_API_KEY", "GLM_API_KEY"),
208	        model="glm-5.2",
209	        base_url="https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4",
210	    ),
211	]

214	@dataclass
215	class LLMResult:
216	    """A completion plus the provenance needed to record it honestly."""
217	
218	    text: str
219	    tier_id: str
220	    provider: str
221	    attempts: int
222	    degraded: bool  # served by something other than the first enabled tier
223	    #: True only when a schema was requested AND the serving tier honoured it.
224	    #:
225	    #: Deliberately not folded into `degraded`, which already means "a tier
226	    #: other than the first served this". Those are different degradations with
227	    #: different fixes — one is a routing fact, the other says the JSON came
228	    #: back on the model's good behaviour rather than under enforcement — and a
229	    #: caller that cannot tell them apart cannot act on either.
230	    schema_enforced: bool = False
231	
232	
233	class AllProvidersFailed(RuntimeError):
234	    """Every enabled tier failed. Carries the per-tier reasons."""
235	
236	    def __init__(self, failures: Dict[str, str]):
237	        self.failures = failures
238	        detail = "; ".join(f"{tier}: {err}" for tier, err in failures.items()) or "no tiers enabled"
239	        super().__init__(f"All LLM providers failed ({detail})")
240	
241	
242	class BudgetExhausted(RuntimeError):
243	    """max_tokens ran out before the model emitted an answer."""
244	
245	
246	class SchemaUnsupported(RuntimeError):
247	    """The tier rejected the structured-output request itself.
248	
249	    Distinct from a failed *call*: the tier is healthy and its credential is
250	    good, it just does not implement `response_format: json_schema` (or the
251	    forced-tool equivalent). Treating this as a tier failure would walk the
252	    whole chain looking for a capability the next tier may not have either,
253	    when retrying this same tier unconstrained is both cheaper and likelier to
254	    work — a schema-less answer that parses beats no answer at all.
255	    """
256	
257	
258	#: Markers in a 400 body that mean "I don't implement structured output",
259	#: as opposed to "your request was bad". Gateways word this differently:
260	#: OpenRouter says the provider doesn't support response_format, others name
261	#: the field directly.
262	_SCHEMA_REJECTION_MARKERS = (
263	    "response_format",
264	    "json_schema",
265	    "structured output",
266	    "does not support",
267	    "unsupported parameter",
268	    "tool_choice",
269	)
270	
271	
272	def _is_schema_rejection(exc: Exception) -> bool:
273	    """True when a 4xx names structured output as the thing it refused.
274	
275	    Deliberately narrow: it must be a client error AND mention the feature.
276	    A generic 400 stays a generic 400, so a genuinely malformed request is not
277	    silently retried as though the schema were at fault.
278	    """
279	    status = _status_of(exc)
280	    if status is not None and not (400 <= status < 500):
281	        return False
282	    body = str(exc).lower()
283	    return any(marker in body for marker in _SCHEMA_REJECTION_MARKERS)
284	
285	
286	#: 400 is ambiguous: "credit balance too low" / "quota exceeded" kills the tier
287	#: for the whole run, but a malformed or oversized single request does not.
288	#: Marking every 400 permanent would let one bad document disable a working
289	#: provider for the remaining 100+ episodes.
290	_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_400 = ("credit balance", "billing", "quota", "insufficient", "payment", "plans & billing")
291	
292	
293	def _is_account_level(exc: Exception) -> bool:
294	    return any(marker in str(exc).lower() for marker in _ACCOUNT_LEVEL_400)
295	
296	
297	def _status_of(exc: Exception) -> Optional[int]:
298	    """Best-effort HTTP status from an SDK exception.
299	
300	    Both the openai and anthropic SDKs raise APIStatusError subclasses
301	    carrying `.status_code`; httpx errors carry `.response.status_code`.
302	    """
303	    status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
304	    if isinstance(status, int):
305	        return status
306	    response = getattr(exc, "response", None)
307	    status = getattr(response, "status_code", None)
308	    return status if isinstance(status, int) else None
309	
310	
311	def _is_permanent(exc: Exception) -> bool:
312	    if isinstance(exc, BudgetExhausted):
313	        return False  # request-level, and retried with a raised ceiling
314	    status = _status_of(exc)
315	    if status == 400:
316	        return _is_account_level(exc)
317	    if status is not None:
318	        return status in PERMANENT_STATUS
319	    # No status: an import failure or client-construction error is permanent;
320	    # a network blip is not.
321	    return isinstance(exc, (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError))
322	
323	
324	def _is_transient(exc: Exception) -> bool:
325	    status = _status_of(exc)
326	    if status is not None:
327	        return status in TRANSIENT_STATUS
328	    return not isinstance(exc, (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError))
329	
330	
331	class LLMFallback:
332	    """Ordered frontier chain with per-tier retry and dead-tier caching."""
333	
334	    def __init__(
335	        self,
336	        tiers: Optional[Sequence[Tier]] = None,
337	        *,
338	        prefer_provider: Optional[str] = None,
339	        backoff_base: float = 0.75,
340	    ):
341	        chain = list(tiers if tiers is not None else FRONTIER_FALLBACK_CHAIN)
342	        prefer = (prefer_provider or os.getenv("RAG_PIPELINE_PROVIDER") or "").lower().strip()
343	        if prefer:
344	            # Stable partition: preferred vendor's tiers first, order preserved.
345	            chain.sort(key=lambda t: 0 if prefer in t.id.lower() else 1)
346	        self.tiers = chain
347	        self.backoff_base = backoff_base
348	        self._dead: Dict[str, str] = {}
349	        self._clients: Dict[str, Any] = {}
350	
351	    # -- introspection ----------------------------------------------------
352	
353	    def enabled_tiers(self) -> List[Tier]:
354	        """Tiers with a credential present and not yet proven dead."""
355	        return [t for t in self.tiers if t.api_key() and t.id not in self._dead]
356	
357	    def describe(self) -> str:
358	        enabled = self.enabled_tiers()
359	        if not enabled:
360	            return "no enabled tiers"
361	        return " -> ".join(t.id for t in enabled)
362	
363	    # -- clients ----------------------------------------------------------
364	
365	    def _client(self, tier: Tier):
366	        if tier.id in self._clients:
367	            return self._clients[tier.id]
368	        key = tier.api_key()
369	        if tier.kind == "anthropic":
370	            from anthropic import Anthropic
371	
372	            client = Anthropic(api_key=key)
373	        else:
374	            from openai import OpenAI
375	
376	            client = OpenAI(api_key=key, base_url=tier.base_url) if tier.base_url else OpenAI(api_key=key)
377	        self._clients[tier.id] = client
378	        return client
379	
380	    def _call_provider(
381	        self,
382	        tier: Tier,
383	        system_prompt: str,
384	        user_content: str,
385	        temperature: float,
386	        max_tokens: int,
387	        schema: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
388	        schema_name: str = "response",
389	        strict: bool = False,
390	    ) -> str:
391	        client = self._client(tier)
392	        if tier.kind == "anthropic":
393	            kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {}
394	            if schema is not None:
395	                # Anthropic has no response_format; a forced tool call is the
396	                # equivalent guarantee — the model must emit arguments matching
397	                # the schema, and we read them back as the JSON body.
398	                kwargs["tools"] = [{
399	                    "name": schema_name,
400	                    "description": "Return the result in this exact structure.",
401	                    "input_schema": schema,
402	                }]
403	                kwargs["tool_choice"] = {"type": "tool", "name": schema_name}
404	            message = client.messages.create(
405	                model=tier.model,
406	                max_tokens=max_tokens,
407	                temperature=temperature,
408	                system=system_prompt,
409	                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_content}],
410	                **kwargs,
411	            )
412	            if schema is not None:
413	                for block in message.content:
414	                    if getattr(block, "type", "") == "tool_use":
415	                        return json.dumps(block.input)
416	                raise SchemaUnsupported(
417	                    f"{tier.id}: forced tool call returned no tool_use block")
418	            return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", "") == "text")
419	
420	        request: Dict[str, Any] = dict(
421	            model=tier.model,
422	            temperature=temperature,
423	            max_tokens=max_tokens,
424	            messages=[
425	                {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
426	                {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
427	            ],
428	        )
429	        if schema is not None:
430	            # OpenAI-compatible structured output. Every tier in the chain is
431	            # reached through an OpenAI-shaped endpoint (OpenRouter, DeepSeek,
432	            # Together, Groq, Ollama), so one request shape covers all of them.
433	            #
434	            # `strict` is opt-in per call site, not hardcoded. Strict mode is a
435	            # *narrower* JSON Schema dialect — every object needs
436	            # `additionalProperties: false` and every property must appear in
437	            # `required` — and a provider that validates the dialect rejects a
438	            # schema that does not comply. Hardcoding it here would mean one
439	            # unhardened schema anywhere could 400 every call through this
440	            # chain. Turn it on per schema, once that schema is known clean.
441	            #
442	            # Measured 2026-08-10: OpenRouter -> z-ai/glm-5.2 accepts strict
443	            # and enforces the field names, but does NOT validate the strict
444	            # dialect (entity.schema.json, which violates it in 10 places, was
445	            # accepted at strict: true). So strict is not self-enforcing here —
446	            # a schema being accepted by tier 1 is not evidence it is clean.
447	            request["response_format"] = {
448	                "type": "json_schema",
449	                "json_schema": {
450	                    "name": schema_name,
451	                    "strict": strict,
452	                    "schema": schema,
453	                },
454	            }
455	        try:
456	            response = client.chat.completions.create(**request)
457	        except Exception as exc:
458	            # A gateway that does not implement json_schema rejects the request
459	            # outright (400). That is a capability gap, not a dead provider —
460	            # raise it distinctly so complete() can retry unconstrained here
461	            # instead of burning the tier and falling down the whole chain.
462	            if schema is not None and _is_schema_rejection(exc):
463	                raise SchemaUnsupported(f"{tier.id}: {exc}") from exc
464	            raise
465	        choice = response.choices[0]
466	        text = choice.message.content or ""
467	        # A reasoning model that ran out of budget returns empty content with
468	        # finish_reason="length" — the answer never got written. Name that
469	        # precisely instead of letting it surface as "provider returned empty
470	        # text", which reads like a dead provider and sends you debugging the
471	        # wrong thing.
472	        if not text.strip() and choice.finish_reason == "length":
473	            raise BudgetExhausted(
474	                f"{tier.id}: max_tokens={max_tokens} consumed before any answer "
475	                f"was emitted (reasoning={tier.reasoning}); raise max_tokens"
476	            )
477	        return text
478	
479	    # -- public API -------------------------------------------------------
480	
481	    def complete(
482	        self,
483	        system_prompt: str,
484	        user_content: str,
485	        *,
486	        temperature: float = DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE,
487	        max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS,
488	        schema: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
489	        schema_name: str = "response",
490	        strict: bool = False,
491	    ) -> LLMResult:
492	        """Run the chain, returning the first success and its provenance.
493	
494	        When `schema` is given, the provider is required to emit JSON matching
495	        it rather than merely asked to in prose. This is what separates a
496	        parseable answer from a hopeful one: the pipeline previously pasted the
497	        schema into the system prompt as text and called json.loads on whatever
498	        came back, so a single malformed comma at char 8455 silently produced
499	        zero chunks, zero NER, and zero embeddable texts while the run still
500	        reported success.
501	
502	        `strict` narrows the schema dialect (see _invoke). Pass it only for a
503	        schema audited against strict's rules; an unaudited schema under strict
504	        is how you 400 a healthy tier.
505	
506	        A tier that cannot honour the schema is not a failed tier — see
507	        SchemaUnsupported. Raises AllProvidersFailed only when every enabled
508	        tier is exhausted.
509	        """
510	        failures: Dict[str, str] = {}
511	        attempts = 0
512	        first_enabled = None
513	
514	        for tier in self.tiers:
515	            if not tier.api_key():
516	                continue  # credential absent — free skip, not a failure
517	            if first_enabled is None:
518	                first_enabled = tier.id
519	            if tier.id in self._dead:
520	                failures.setdefault(tier.id, f"skipped ({self._dead[tier.id]})")
521	                continue
522	
523	            # Reasoning tiers bill chain-of-thought against max_tokens, so a
524	            # budget sized for a non-reasoning model yields a truncated or
525	            # empty answer. Add headroom rather than raising a floor: the
526	            # caller's number sizes the answer, not the model's thinking.
527	            tier_max_tokens = (
528	                max_tokens + REASONING_HEADROOM_TOKENS if tier.reasoning else max_tokens
529	            )
530	
531	            for attempt in range(1, tier.max_retries + 2):
532	                attempts += 1
533	                try:
534	                    try:
535	                        text = self._call_provider(
536	                            tier, system_prompt, user_content, temperature, tier_max_tokens,
537	                            schema=schema, schema_name=schema_name, strict=strict,
538	                        )
539	                        enforced = schema is not None
540	                    except SchemaUnsupported as exc:
541	                        # The tier is healthy and its credential is good — it
542	                        # just does not implement structured output. Retry it
543	                        # unconstrained rather than descending: the next tier
544	                        # may not implement it either, and a schema-less answer
545	                        # that parses beats no answer. Caught here, ahead of the
546	                        # generic handler below, because _is_permanent says
547	                        # False and _is_transient says True for this exception —
548	                        # so falling through would retry the same tier with the
549	                        # same schema and then burn the rest of the chain.
550	                        logger.warning(
551	                            "LLM tier %s does not support structured output (%s) — "
552	                            "retrying unconstrained on the same tier", tier.id, exc,
553	                        )
554	                        attempts += 1
555	                        text = self._call_provider(
556	                            tier, system_prompt, user_content, temperature, tier_max_tokens,
557	                        )
558	                        enforced = False
559	                    if not text.strip():
560	                        raise RuntimeError("provider returned empty text")
561	                    if tier.id != first_enabled:
562	                        logger.info("LLM fallback: served by %s (degraded from %s)", tier.id, first_enabled)
563	                    return LLMResult(
564	                        text=text,
565	                        tier_id=tier.id,
566	                        provider=tier.provider,
567	                        attempts=attempts,
568	                        degraded=tier.id != first_enabled,
569	                        schema_enforced=enforced,
570	                    )
571	                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified below
572	                    reason = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
573	                    failures[tier.id] = reason
574	                    if _is_permanent(exc):
575	                        status = _status_of(exc)
576	                        self._dead[tier.id] = f"HTTP {status}" if status else type(exc).__name__
577	                        logger.warning(
578	                            "LLM tier %s permanently unavailable (%s) — skipping for the rest of this run",
579	                            tier.id, self._dead[tier.id],
580	                        )
581	                        break
582	                    last_attempt = attempt >= tier.max_retries + 1
583	                    if isinstance(exc, BudgetExhausted) and not last_attempt:
584	                        tier_max_tokens *= 2
585	                        logger.warning(
586	                            "LLM tier %s exhausted its token budget — retrying at max_tokens=%d",
587	                            tier.id, tier_max_tokens,
588	                        )
589	                        continue
590	                    if last_attempt or not _is_transient(exc):
591	                        logger.warning("LLM tier %s failed (%s) — trying next tier", tier.id, reason)
592	                        break
```

```text
"""Bridge to packages/ai/prompts YAML registry for disclosure-rag."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _resolve_prompts_dir() -> Path:
    env = os.getenv("PROMPTS_DIR")
    if env:
        return Path(env)

    candidates = [
        _REPO_ROOT / "packages" / "ai" / "prompts",
        _REPO_ROOT / "packages" / "prompts",  # legacy
    ]
    for cand in candidates:
        if cand.exists() and (cand / "registry.yaml").exists():
            return cand

    # Prefer ai/prompts even if missing so import errors are clear
    return _REPO_ROOT / "packages" / "ai" / "prompts"


_PROMPTS_DIR = _resolve_prompts_dir()
if str(_PROMPTS_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_PROMPTS_DIR))

from prompt_helpers import get_prompt, get_prompt_with_schema  # noqa: E402
from yaml_loader import list_prompts  # noqa: E402

__all__ = ["get_prompt", "get_prompt_with_schema",
           "PROMPTS_DIR", "list_registered_prompts"]

PROMPTS_DIR = _PROMPTS_DIR


def list_registered_prompts():
    """Return registry entries from packages/ai/prompts."""
    return list_prompts(str(PROMPTS_DIR))
```

```text
"""Single definition of "did LLM enrichment actually happen on this run?".

Every ingestion path produces a `rag_pipeline` block, but files it in a
different place, so grading it needs one search order that knows all of them.
This lived inside scripts/playlist_ingestion.py, where only the playlist path
could reach it — main.py's direct `dy <url>` path had no gate at all and
reported success on a run whose retrieval layer came back empty.

main.py cannot import from scripts/ (playlist_ingestion imports main, so it
would be circular), which is why this is a lib module rather than a helper
shared by proximity.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, Tuple

#: Statuses from RagPipelineResult that mean enrichment genuinely succeeded.
OK_STATUSES = {"ok"}
#: Statuses that are a deliberate, recorded decision — not a failure.
HELD_STATUSES = {"hold", "rejected", "skipped"}


def enrichment_outcome(result: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """Grade LLM enrichment from a process_url/process_file result.

    Returns (status, error_detail).

    The status lives in a different place depending on which path ran:
    `process_file` sets `result['rag_pipeline']` and
    `result['metadata']['rag_pipeline']`; the YouTube path (lib/youtube.py)
    files it under the transcript's file metadata and
    knowledge_base_service surfaces it at both levels.

    Returns "unknown" when no signal is found. That matters: reporting
    `ingested` on absence is precisely how a run of documents whose enrichment
    had 401'd got recorded as successful.
    """
    for container in (result, result.get("metadata") or {}, result.get("file_metadata") or {}):
        rag = container.get("rag_pipeline") if isinstance(container, dict) else None
        if isinstance(rag, dict) and rag.get("status"):
            return rag["status"], "; ".join(rag.get("errors") or [])[:300]

    for stage in result.get("stage_report") or []:
        if isinstance(stage, dict) and "RAG prompt pipeline" in (stage.get("name") or ""):
            raw = stage.get("status") or "unknown"
            return {"success": "ok", "failed": "error"}.get(raw, raw), (stage.get("detail") or "")[:300]

    return "unknown", ""
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
86	def _extract_json_payload(text: str) -> Any:
87	    """Parse JSON from a model response, tolerating markdown fences."""
88	    if not text:

90	
91	    stripped = text.strip()
92	    fence = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*([\s\S]*?)```", stripped, re.IGNORECASE)
93	    if fence:
94	        stripped = fence.group(1).strip()
```

```text
114	        self,

116	        max_ner_chunks: int = MAX_NER_CHUNKS,

126	        self._llm = get_fallback(self.prefer_provider or None)
127	        # Provenance of the tiers that actually served this run, so callers can
128	        # tell real enrichment from silent degradation.
129	        self.tiers_used: List[str] = []

133	        #: Prompts that needed a parse-repair round trip to return valid JSON.
134	        self.repaired_prompts: List[str] = []
135	        logger.info("LLM fallback chain: %s", self._llm.describe())
136
```

Another Claude session sent a message:
<teammate-message teammate_id="salvage" color="yellow" summary="Playlist ingestion assessment: nothing usable is in RAG">
READ-ONLY assessment complete. No files edited, no ingestion re-run, no writes. Bottom line: both "ingested" docs are pipeline failures with zero RAG payload, and the pipeline has no resume-from-transcript capability — a retry re-does everything.

## 1. DB verification result

**The pipeline's own target (per its .env) is a LOCAL Postgres, not the shared Neon DB.** `lib/db/postgres_client.py:get_database_url()` reads `DATABASE_URL` from `apps/disclosure-rag/.env` first; that value resolves to `postgresql://liamellis@localhost:5432/ultraterrestrial` (confirmed via `SELECT current_database(), inet_server_addr()` → `('ultraterrestrial', ::1)`, 76 tables). I initially assumed this was the shared Neon DB (the code's own docstring claims it "must point at the shared Neon endpoint... same database apps/app reads") — it doesn't, in practice, because the local .env overrides it.

Queried both candidate stores by `id = 'K4gYHs84BIc'` / `'uVVqFg2v7ro'`:
- **Local `ultraterrestrial` DB** (what the pipeline actually writes to): `documents` = 0 rows total, `document_chunks` = 0 rows total. Neither doc_id present (trivially — tables are empty).
- **Shared Neon `neondb`** (`packages/db/.env`, confirmed via `current_database()`='neondb', 30 tables — matches root CLAUDE.md's "30 tables, 126,483 records" exactly): `documents` = 189 rows, `document_chunks` = 4,946 rows (matches CLAUDE.md's "4,946 document chunks" exactly, confirming this is the real production DB). Neither doc_id present by `id` or by `url ILIKE '%videoid%'`.
- disclosure-rag's own `NEON_DATABASE_URL` (a third, separate Neon project "ultraterrestrial_owner@...ultraterrestrial") — connection failed, "No route to host" (network-unreachable from this environment). **UNVERIFIED** — could not check this one.

**So: neither doc exists in any Postgres store I could reach.** Not a store-mismatch artifact — I also checked the actual file-level artifacts each run produced, and they explain why:

- `packages/knowledge-base/sources/transcripts/2026-08-06/K4gYHs84BIc/..._rag_pipeline.json`: `"status": "error"`, `chunks: []`, `ner_results: []`, `embeddable_texts: []`, `embeddable_count: 0`. Real transcript + a genuine LLM analysis pass exists (8 extracted claims in `analysis._raw_list`), but the pipeline stage that would produce chunks/NER/embeddings never completed.
- `.../uVVqFg2v7ro/..._rag_pipeline.json`: `"status": "error"`, everything empty, explicit cause: `"All LLM providers failed: Error code: 401 - Incorrect API key provided"` — OpenAI key was dead for this run.
- Both `entity_processing_results.json` files report `"status": "completed"` but every entity category (`topics, personnel, events, organizations, locations, artifacts, sightings`) is an empty array — zero entities either way.

**Quality-gate leak, but not the one implied.** uVVqFg2v7ro's fidelity 0.5/"review" is not a real content-quality signal — its `.fidelity.json` shows `subscores: {}`, `covered_seconds: 0.0`, and `issues: ["Fidelity review error: 'FetchedTranscriptSnippet' object has no attribute 'get'"]` — the fidelity reviewer itself crashed on this file's transcript-segment type and fell back to a default score. The transcript is actually large and fine (25,691 words). Real leak: **`state.json` calls K4gYHs84BIc "ingested" with `rag_status: "unknown"` despite its own `rag_pipeline.json` on disk saying `status: "error"`.** Root cause is in `lib/enrichment_status.py::enrichment_outcome()` — it only detects an error status if the in-memory `result` dict it receives exposes a `rag_pipeline.status` key; for this doc it evidently didn't, so the gate fell through to `"unknown"`, and the code treats `"unknown"` as "not a failure" (`if rag_status not in ("ok", "unknown")`). The file written to disk knew the real status; the in-memory result that graded the run didn't.

**Net: "ingested" (2/104) currently means "wrote transcript + a text summary to local disk files," not "retrievable via RAG." Zero of the 104 videos in this playlist run produced a single chunk, embedding, or entity row anywhere I could verify.**

## 2. Transcript asset inventory

49 `.txt` files under `corpus/intake/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/`:
- `wc -c *.txt`: **7,393,554 bytes total** (~7.05 MiB)
- `wc -w *.txt`: **1,383,742 words total**
- Per-file size (bytes): min 52,835 (`zjpvfDFc4fg.txt`), median 150,002, max 287,702 (`Y7PLeu5rTv4.txt`), mean 150,889
- Per-file word_count (from fidelity reports, `wc -w` cross-check on min not needed since fidelity.json already reports it): min 8,834 (`zjpvfDFc4fg`), median 27,549, max 54,485
- No degenerate files. Spot-checked `zjpvfDFc4fg.txt` (smallest, 8,834 words, `head -c ~2KB`) — coherent documentary-style prose transcript, not truncated or boilerplate; its fidelity report shows 3,817.1s covered at 138.9 wpm, consistent with a genuinely shorter/denser episode, not a failed fetch.
- Scanned all 49 `.fidelity.json` `artifact_ratio`/`repetition_ratio` fields for outliers (>0.02): **none found** — max artifact_ratio and repetition_ratio across the set stay near 0.

## 3. What the fidelity gate measures

--
328:## Playlist Ingestion (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py`)
329-
330:Batch-ingest one or more YouTube podcast playlists end-to-end. Each episode flows through: enumeration → transcript fetch → parse/clean → **fidelity review** (quality gate) → `main.process_url()` (KB storage, RagPromptPipeline sidecars, NER, optional vectorization / CocoIndex / Mem0).
331-
332-```bash
333:# One or more playlist URLs (plain video URLs also accepted)
334:.venv/bin/python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py "https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL..." [MORE_URLS...]
335-
336-# From a file (one URL per line, # comments allowed), with vector store upload
337:.venv/bin/python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py --from-file playlists.txt --upload
338-
339:# Preview a new playlist's caption quality without ingesting
340:.venv/bin/python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --limit 5 --dry-run
341-
342-# Stricter gate + LLM coherence pass (FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL, default gpt-5.5)
343:.venv/bin/python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --min-fidelity 0.6 --llm-review
344-```
345-
346:Flags: `--upload` (OpenAI vector store), `--no-kb`, `--limit N` (per playlist), `--force` (reprocess done episodes), `--dry-run`, `--min-fidelity 0.45`, `--llm-review`, `--delay 2.0` (seconds between episodes), `--state-file PATH`.
347-
348:**Resume is automatic**: state is checkpointed to `data/playlist_ingestion/state.json` after every episode; re-runs skip `ingested`/`quarantined`/`unavailable` episodes and retry `failed`/`no_transcript`/`blocked` ones. After `YT_BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD` consecutive IP blocks (default 3), the run aborts.
349-
350:**Fidelity review** (`lib/transcript_fidelity.py`) scores each transcript 0–1 from coverage, speech density (wpm), caption gaps, artifact ratio, and repetition; verdicts: `pass` ≥ 0.7, `review` ≥ 0.45, `fail` < 0.45. Failing/below-threshold episodes are **quarantined** (transcript + fidelity JSON kept on disk, not ingested). Artifacts: cleaned transcripts in `data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/`, per-episode fidelity reports and per-run markdown summaries in `data/playlist_ingestion/reports/`.
351-
352:See [Playlist ingestion details](references/playlist-ingestion.md) for stage internals, state schema, quarantine review workflow, and tuning.
353-

355-
356-YouTube: URL contains `youtube.com` or `youtu.be`. Web: starts with `http(s)://`. File: everything else (validated with `os.path.exists`).
